input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV is the only renewal provision. It gives the Licensor a unilateral option to extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years, with no exit right, notice window or price protection for us. A vendor-controlled multi-year renewal is walk-away territory under the rule (worse than an automatic renewal, since we have no opt-out at all) and it also contradicts sub-clauses II and III, which contemplate extension only by mutual written agreement. The redline conforms the renewal sentence to the preferred position: 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement with renewal uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. A 12-month auto-renewal with a 30-day (fallback 60-day) opt-out would also be acceptable.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for successive additional periods of twelve (12) months only by mutual written agreement of the parties, and any increase in fees for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding period and three percent (3%).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the Licensor's unilateral seven-year renewal option with twelve-month renewals by mutual written agreement and a CPI/3% cap on renewal fee increases, consistent with the rest of Article IV, which already provides that extensions are by mutual written agreement. Our playbook does not accept multi-year renewals that we cannot exit; we can discuss a 12-month auto-renewal with a 30-day opt-out as an alternative.
proposal.summary: Renewal limited to 12 months by mutual agreement with capped uplift
